name_note: GTDB's Senimuribacter holds the species named Senimuribacter intestinalis and the species described in the literature as Emergencia timonensis, which GTDB calls Senimuribacter timonensis.

sentences.text: Senimuribacter is a bacterial genus that phylogenomic analysis placed in the family Anaerovoracaceae, reassigned together with several related taxa from the family Eubacteriaceae.
A study of two butyrate-producing strains from mouse faeces reported high 16S rRNA gene similarity to Senimuribacter intestinalis, a named species of this genus.
The species GTDB calls Senimuribacter timonensis was isolated from human stools by culturomics and proposed as the new genus and species Emergencia timonensis.
A study reported that the human gut bacterium Emergencia timonensis converts the L-carnitine-derived metabolite gamma-butyrobetaine to trimethylamine using an induced gene cluster.
Another study reported that adding Emergencia timonensis to gnotobiotic mice completed the carnitine to trimethylamine route, raised TMAO and enhanced thrombosis potential after arterial injury.
